label: prop:markov-pair-z2
title: All-pairs Markov-trace identity $\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i\sigma_j) = z^2$
html:
Let H_n(R, q) be the Iwahori--Hecke algebra with Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M normalised by \mathrm{tr}_M(1_k) = 1 for all k and Markov axiom \mathrm{tr}_M(x\sigma_{k-1}) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) for x \in H_{k-1}(q), where z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) (convention D, Jones--Markov trace).

Proposition. For every pair of braid generators \sigma_i, \sigma_j with 0 \le i < j, embedded in any H_n(R, q) with n > j,

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i\sigma_j) \;=\; z^2.

The identity holds whether (i,j) are adjacent (j = i+1) or non-adjacent (j \ge i+2).

Operator interpretation

Retracted and replaced, 2026-08-09. This section read:

The value z^2 is the Jones polynomial of the Hopf link (unknotted two-component linking) evaluated at the substrate parameter: J_{\mathrm{Hopf}}(q) = -(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})\cdot z^2 = -(q + q^{-1})/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}).

That is wrong three times over, and only the third is about the convention.

  1. Wrong link. z^2 = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i\sigma_j). The closure of \sigma_1\sigma_2 in B_3 is the unknot; the closure of \sigma_1\sigma_3 in B_4 is the two-component unlink. Neither is the Hopf link, which is the closure of \sigma_1^2 in B_2 and has trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^2) = hz + 1, not z^2.
  2. Wrong kind of object. A raw Markov-trace value is not a Jones polynomial. Without the loop factor \delta^{\,n-1} and the framing correction it is not even an invariant of the closure — it changes under Markov stabilisation, which is exactly what z measures.
  3. Wrong loop parameter. q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2} is [2]_{\sqrt q} = 2.0027\ldots at q_0; the Temperley–Lieb loop value of the production trace is \delta = [2]_q = q+q^{-1} = 2.010896866707122\ldots — the same conflation as 1/\delta = 0.4972905456\ldots against the excised z_{\mathrm{C}} = 0.4993203342\ldots.

The correct normalisation. For \beta \in B_n with exponent sum e,

  V_{\hat\beta}(t) \;=\; q^{-2e}\,[2]_q^{\,n-1}\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta),
  \qquad t = q^{-2},

with no square roots anywhere. The reason is that under convention D the element e_i := q - \sigma_i is a Temperley–Lieb generator,

  e_i^2 \;=\; q^2 - 2q\sigma_i + \sigma_i^2 \;=\; (q^2+1) - (q+q^{-1})\sigma_i
       \;=\; [2]_q\,e_i ,

and convention D is precisely the statement that \mathrm{tr}_M(e_i) = 1/\delta:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(e_i) = q - z, \qquad (q-z)\,[2]_q = 1 .

So \mathrm{tr}_M is not merely compatible with the Jones–Temperley–Lieb trace — written in e_i it is that trace, which is what the registry name "SU(2)/Temperley–Lieb (Jones) decomposition" means as an identity. The Kauffman variable is A^2 = -q, giving \delta = -A^2-A^{-2} and t = A^{-4} = q^{-2}; the odd powers of A in \rho(\sigma_i) = (A/q)\sigma_i cancel against the writhe factor (-A^3)^{-e}, leaving q^{-2e}.

Four closures, computed from the formula and checked against their known Jones polynomials:

closure braid e n \mathrm{tr}_M V from the formula known
unknot \widehat{\sigma_1}, B_2 1 2 z 1 1
unknot \widehat{\sigma_1\sigma_2}, B_3 2 3 z^2 1 1
Hopf link \widehat{\sigma_1^2}, B_2 2 2 hz+1 = \tfrac{q^4+1}{q^2+1} q^{-1}+q^{-5} -t^{1/2}-t^{5/2}
2-unlink \widehat{\sigma_1\sigma_3}, B_4 2 4 z^2 [2]_q -t^{1/2}-t^{-1/2}

The last two rows are the point. Rows 2 and 4 have the same trace value z^2 and different links; only n distinguishes them. Any account that reads a Jones polynomial off a raw trace value cannot tell them apart at all — which is how the retracted sentence came to call the unknot a Hopf link.

For the Hopf row the sign sits entirely in the branch of t^{1/2}: with t^{1/2} := A^{-2} = -q^{-1}, -t^{1/2}-t^{5/2} = q^{-1}+q^{-5}. In q there is no ambiguity, which is one practical reason to state the normalisation in q.

Why this is a link invariant, and why D is the only choice. The table above would be worth little if it rested on knowing which link each braid closes to. It does not. By Markov's theorem, two braids have the same closure exactly when they are related by conjugation and by stabilisation \beta \in B_n \mapsto \beta\sigma_n^{\pm 1} \in B_{n+1}, so invariance under those moves is the statement that V is a link invariant — and all three checks are algebra, with no knot theory in them:

move effect invariance condition
conjugation e, n fixed; \mathrm{tr}_M cyclic automatic, any z
positive stabilisation e \mapsto e+1, n \mapsto n+1, \mathrm{tr}_M \mapsto z\,\mathrm{tr}_M q^{-2}[2]_q\,z = 1
negative stabilisation e \mapsto e-1, n \mapsto n+1, \mathrm{tr}_M \mapsto (z-h)\,\mathrm{tr}_M q^{2}[2]_q\,(z-h) = 1

(The negative row uses \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - h, which follows from the quadratic relation alone: \sigma(\sigma - h) = \sigma^2 - h\sigma = 1.)

Each stabilisation condition is not merely satisfied by convention D — each one, on its own, forces it, needing only q \neq 0. Hence:

Convention D is the unique Markov parameter for which q^{-2e}[2]_q^{\,n-1}\mathrm{tr}_M is a link invariant.

That the two stabilisations independently pin the same z is a genuine consistency check on the normalisation, not a restatement — and it passes.

Under this statement the retracted prefactor q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2} is not a near-miss. With it the quantity fails to survive a stabilisation move, so it is not an invariant of anything at all.

Proved in JonesNormalisation.lean — tl_generator_sq, sigma_inv, stab_pos_iff_conventionD, stab_neg_iff_conventionD, jonesV_stabilise_pos, jonesV_stabilise_neg, conventionD_iff_markov_invariant, plus the four closure values (unknot_two_strand, unknot_three_strand, hopf_link, two_component_unlink) and kauffman_loop. Sorry-free; every hypothesis is IsConventionD plus q \neq 0, and q^2+1 \neq 0 is derived rather than assumed (q_sq_add_one_ne_zero) — in a general field it can vanish, so assuming it would have been a hidden hypothesis.

The four closure rows are retained as sanity checks — they confirm the invariant is normalised so the unknot is 1 — but they are no longer load-bearing.

The proposition above is unaffected. \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i\sigma_j) = z^2 follows from the Markov axiom alone and holds for any Markov parameter. So the pair blow-up centre at coordinate \hat V_i\hat V_j still carries weight z^2 regardless of its position in the braid, matching the empirically-verified all-pairs set on atoms A \ge 6 (cf. adjacent-vs-full-canonical evaluation.witness.json, jet-tower remark). Only the knot-theoretic gloss was wrong.

The proposition is convention-independent; the Hopf-link normalisation above is not, and has NOT been re-derived. Flagged 2026-08-09, not fixed.

\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i\sigma_j) = z^2 follows from the Markov axiom alone and holds for any Markov parameter, so switching z to convention D (z = q^3/(q^2+1), as the cited theorem now states) leaves the proposition untouched.

The normalisation J_{\mathrm{Hopf}}(q) = -(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2})\cdot z^2 is a different matter. Its prefactor is the loop parameter at half argument, [2]_{\sqrt q} = q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2} = 2.0027\ldots at q_0, whereas the Temperley–Lieb loop value of the production trace is \delta = [2]_q = q + q^{-1} = 2.010896866707122\ldots — a 0.4\% difference, and the two are conflated across the corpus (the reciprocal 1/\delta = 0.497290545604915556 against z_C = 0.499320334183694452 is the same confusion). The identity was derived when z was z_C, and under convention D — which is the Jones/Temperley–Lieb trace — both the prefactor and z^2 change, so the displayed second equality -(q+q^{-1})/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}) cannot be assumed to survive.

Deliberately left as-is rather than patched: getting the Jones normalisation right under D is a derivation, not a substitution, and quietly editing the prefactor would produce a formula nobody has checked. Bean qou-98g5 (δ vs z_C conflation) and qou-emyt.
